findings.description: When no driver is armed but the inverse `read-tree` itself fails, the printed fallback now says only ". Put it back with:". The old order to clear `filter.*` and `info/attributes` before pasting is gone. Decision 80, rewritten in this same commit, says the line is printed with that order "as it is when the inverse fails".
findings.body:
**The restore line printed for a later paste no longer says to clear drivers first.**

At 97c7fd8, the fallback always said *"Clear any filter.\* config and info/attributes first (decision 50), then put it back with:"*. Now that order appears only in the `armed.length > 0` branch. If no driver is armed but `checkout(inverse)` throws, the message says only `. Put it back with:` and gives the command.

That case is reachable: the inverse two-way `read-tree -m -u` refuses whenever a file it would rewrite has a local change in the main checkout.

The `armed` value is a snapshot taken inside the catch. The operator pastes the command later, while sessions are still alive. In that gap a session can arm a `filter.<x>.smudge` plus `info/attributes`. The pasted `read-tree -u` then runs that filter on every file it rewrites, as the operator.

The printed `git` prefix can't prevent this. It sets only `core.hooksPath`, `core.fsmonitor` and `submodule.recurse`. The `armedGitDrivers` JSDoc (`git-diff.client.ts` L323-326) says smudge filters have no `-c` disarm. So the clear-first instruction is the only protection this line offers.

The code also contradicts decision 80 as rewritten in this commit (`docs/09-decisions.md` ~L4070-4073): "…the line is printed with the order to clear `filter.*` and `info/attributes` first (decision 50), **as it is when the inverse fails**."

**Fix:** in the not-armed branch, keep decision 50's order, e.g. `. Clear any filter.* config and info/attributes first (decision 50), then put it back with:\n`.

findings.description: Returning `[]` on a detached checkout looks exactly like a real sweep that found nothing. So the watch loop prints "clear — no overlaps" while the stored overlaps are still there and nothing was scanned.
findings.body:
**On a detached main checkout, `pup watch` now reports "clear — no overlaps" even though nothing was scanned.**

The fix keeps the stored overlaps and withholds the beat, which is right for `pup status`. But `if (!target) return [];` gives the only caller the same value a real empty sweep gives.

In `pup watch` (`src/cli/index.ts` L1273-1305), the snapshot is `JSON.stringify({ pairs, stalledIds })`. With `pairs = []` and no stalled session, L1303-1304 print `${stamp}  clear — no overlaps`. That happens:
- on the first sweep, and with `--once`;
- whenever the checkout detaches after a sweep that had found overlaps.

The loop never reads the stored overlaps or the beat, so the operator gets a positive all-clear exactly while the radar is blind. Ordinary actions trigger this: `git checkout <sha>`, a bisect, or an interactive rebase on the main checkout.

The comment at index.ts L1279-1281 ("the overlap scan above has already recorded this sweep's beat") is also no longer always true.

**Fix:** let the caller tell a skipped sweep from an empty one. For example, return `undefined` (or throw) on a detached checkout, and have the watch loop print something like `radar paused — main checkout is detached` instead of the clear line. Update the L1279-1281 comment to match.

findings.description: The bare `catch { return 'nowhere' }` also swallows `resolveCommit`'s symbolic-ref refusal. A target turned into a symref after the pin is now reported as "moved from X to nowhere" instead of "is a symbolic ref to Y … Treat a session that wrote it as compromised". It still refuses, but it misnames the state and drops the compromise warning.

`armedGitDrivers` runs unguarded inside the catch. If it throws, for example because a session made the config unparseable or turned `info/attributes` into a directory (EISDIR), its error replaces the whole report. The operator loses the update-ref failure, the note that the checkout holds `${sha}`'s files, and the paste line.

The new `!target` early return cites "(decision 80)" for the detached-checkout skip. The decision 80 text in `docs/09-decisions.md` (edited in this delta) says nothing about skipping the overlap sweep or withholding the beat when the main checkout is detached. It only covers the `refs/heads/` naming for review and overlap, the second driver check, and the restore.
The four-line comment partly narrates what the code does ("Skipped whole instead") alongside the WHY.
The comment above the detached-checkout test restates the test name, which already says 'skips the sweep on a detached main checkout, keeping overlaps and withholding the beat'.

The failure message now nests a ternary (`restored ? … : …`) around a second ternary (`armed.length > 0 ? … : …`). That is three message variants built by string concatenation inside one `throw`, which is hard to read and to test branch by branch.

`fastForward` wraps `resolveCommit` in an inline IIFE with try/catch to turn a deleted target into the string `'nowhere'`, and the restore block just below it gets a second IIFE-style `let restored` flow.

The literal `refs/heads/${target}` is now built inline in about 12 places across `merge-gate.service.ts`, `review.service.ts`, `overlap.service.ts` and `conductor.service.ts`. This diff adds two more in `conductor.service.ts` (lines 82 and 91) and re-adds one in `merge-gate.service.ts`.
